articles.title: How Birbhum's job-guarantee money was frozen for four years
articles.dek: West Bengal's MGNREGS funds were halted at the source from March 2022. A rural district shows what happens when money is withheld from the top — not misspent at the bottom.
articles.author: Ankur Sinha
articles.body:
Most stories about misused public money follow a familiar shape: funds arrive, and they are spent badly. Birbhum, a rural district in West Bengal, shows the **opposite** failure — money that never arrived at all.

## The freeze

From **9 March 2022**, the Union government stopped releasing MGNREGS funds to West Bengal under **Section 27 of the MGNREGA Act**, citing non-compliance. The rural job-guarantee scheme — the wage floor for millions — went dry across the state. For an MGNREGS-dependent district like Birbhum, that meant unpaid wages, unbuilt assets, and migration.

## What piled up

By 2025, the Centre's own figure in the Rajya Sabha put pending MGNREGS dues to West Bengal at **₹3,038 crore** — the highest of any state. The state's claim across MGNREGS and PMAY-G ran far higher.

## Why it matters

This is the federal-friction axis made concrete: a State-implemented, Union-funded scheme, switched off upstream. Work resumed only in **June 2026**, after Supreme Court intervention. Whether you read the freeze as a justified anti-corruption measure or as political leverage, the **structure** is the story — and it is the same structure that decides whether money reaches every other district.

See the full dated chain on the [timeline](timeline.html), and Birbhum's ledger on the [map](index.html?state=West%20Bengal&district=Birbhum).
